The revised first sentence reports non-admission under current image-size rules, not actual OOM or insufficient RAM allowance.

ImportMemoryRequirements.accepts combines ImageMemoryPolicy.accepts with the decoded-array cap and estimated byte use. ImageMemoryPolicy.accepts requires target pixels <= maxPixels(residentPixels), decodedPixels <= MAX_BITMAP_PIXELS and plan estimates <= workingBytes; maxPixels itself is min(MAX_BITMAP_PIXELS, permitted RAM-derived pixels). Thus a hard bitmap/array cap can reject a size even when the RAM comparison would pass. The revised rule/not-usable wording covers every one of these predicates without choosing a cause.

Reduce dimensions OR cancel this operation and free RAM are both retained verbatim. The latter is an alternative instruction to make RAM unused, not an assertion that RAM shortage caused this particular refusal or that releasing RAM would cure a hard cap.

cannotResize being false does not certify that another size fits: for non-native requirements it can be false even when the 1x1 probe fails. No successful retry, actual resize, automatic release, input damage or whole-image loss is claimed.
